description:
About the Position

The Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in biochemistry. The department conducts fundamental research on the molecular machinery of life, spanning enzyme mechanisms, membrane proteins, RNA biology and cellular metabolism, using approaches that connect structural, biochemical and cell-biological methods. The doctoral position is a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement, based at the university's Albano campus within the Stockholm life-science environment.

Doctoral students design their projects with the supervisory team, receive training through the university's doctoral programmes, and present their work in departmental seminars and international conferences. Stockholm University ranks among Europe's strong research universities in molecular biosciences, and the department hosts well-equipped core facilities and collaborates closely with the surrounding Science for Life Laboratory environment. The position suits a candidate aiming for a research career in molecular life sciences.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, chemistry or a related field, with laboratory experience in protein science or molecular methods. Selection weighs academic record, research experience, motivation and fit with the project. Applications run through Stockholm University's Varbi portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a personal letter, and shortlisted candidates are interviewed before admission decisions.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD employment in biochemistry
  • Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics, Stockholm University
  • Enzyme, membrane-protein and metabolism research
  • Structural and cell-biological methods with core facilities
  • Stockholm life-science and SciLifeLab environment
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

About Stockholm University

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
